claim: Input-referred threshold (offset) of the sky130 differential receiver under local device mismatch (Monte Carlo, vary=mismatch, `*_mm` library sections) at common-mode 0.8, 1.65 and 2.5 V, at tt (27 C, 3.3 V) and at the binding corner of the 45-point record (sf, 100 C, 3.0 V), against spec/usb2-phy.md section 6 row 'Differential input sensitivity' |(D+) - (D-)| > 200 mV (threshold strictly inside (-200 mV, +200 mV) and the output a valid logic level at VDIFF = +/-200 mV). Schematic-level, no layout parasitics; not a signoff or catalog-tier claim.

corners.basis: binding corner of the 45-point record sim/diff-receiver-sensitivity/records/20261009-121939-0555da1.md: the largest |vth| (-75.97 mV, vth_cm2p50_v) is at sf / 100 C / 3.00 V

control.description: fixed 0.25 V differential input offset (equivalent input-referred input-pair Vth skew, split across DP and DM) via the testbench skew_v parameter

record.netlist_provenance: schematic-derived netlist: xschem export of design/differential_receiver.sch (design/netlist/differential_receiver.spice) plus the Monte Carlo testbench deck, frozen per campaign; no layout, no parasitic extraction
record.statistical_convention: Monte Carlo of local device mismatch only (monte_carlo.vary = mismatch): n = 400 samples per corner, base seed 166, per-sample seeds derived by `klt sim` (seed contract: sim.md 'Monte Carlo sampling'); every MOS and res_xhigh_po_1p41 instance draws independent mismatch (mc_mm_switch = 1 through the `*_mm` library sections); global process spread is the separate corner axis (tt and sf here, plus the 45- and 225-point deterministic records) and is not sampled
method: Stimulus and measurements as sim/diff-receiver-sensitivity (VDIFF = DP - DM swept -400 ... +400 mV at 1 mV, VCM in {0.8, 1.65, 2.5} V, one receiver instance per VCM), with the supply, temperature and library section of the corner and the extra `skew_v` input-pair offset parameter (0 in the nominal campaign).

Row measurements per VCM: `vth_*` = first VDIFF at which RXD crosses VDD/2, must lie strictly inside (-200 mV, +200 mV); `rxd_p200_*` / `rxd_m200_*` = RXD at VDIFF = +/-200 mV, must be >= 0.9 x VDD / <= 0.1 x VDD of the corner supply (a valid logic level at the row limit). A sample with no crossing in +/-400 mV has no `vth` and is reported by klt yield as `errored`; the lint requires errored = 0 for a PASS record.

Each corner is its own population (one `klt sim` Monte Carlo request, backend batch, per corner); nothing is pooled across corners. `klt yield-samples` pairs each nominal campaign with its negative-control campaign (same deck, same seeds, the deterministic skew below), and `klt yield` grades the pair against the row limits with target_yield 0.99 at 95 % confidence.

Negative control (deterministic): the control campaign applies a fixed 0.25 V differential input offset (`skew_v`), which moves every sample's differential threshold to about -0.28 ... -0.33 V, past the 200 mV row. The yield report must flag it `detected` for every measurement; a campaign whose control is `not_detected` cannot be a PASS record.

Mismatch activity: `klt sim --dry-run` reports mosfet and resistor mismatch as active for `*_mm` sections; the per-sample spread of `vth_*` in the report (stddev in each yield report's `distribution`) is the evidence that mismatch reached the g5v0d10v5 devices used here (a stddev of zero would fail the record).
PDK: the pinned open_pdks revision of sim/pdk-pins.json (current pin); each record states the revision and the model library sha256.
record.footer: Scope: schematic-level statistical evidence for one block against the ratified differential-sensitivity row, at the corners named in the record. Local device mismatch only; global process spread is covered by the deterministic corner records, and the corner x mismatch combination is limited to the two corners named. It does not claim layout, DRC/LVS, level shifting or signoff, and does not relax any target. A FAIL record is evidence of failure, not compliance.

yield.sample_size_justification: target_yield 0.99 at 95 % two-sided confidence: with zero observed failures the exact (Clopper-Pearson) lower bound reaches 0.99 only for n >= 368 (klt yield `required_n_for_target`), so n = 400 per corner is the smallest round count that can support the claim; the +/-0.01 precision target needs n >= 183. A failing row is not rescued by a larger n: it is recorded as failing.
